claims.text: The initial near-equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy is a single-phase, fine-grained solid solution.
Aging near-equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi at approximately 500°C causes a transition from nanoscale chemical ordering to coarsened clusters or secondary precipitates as aging time increases.
Aging for less than 2 hours at approximately 500°C facilitates subtle nanoscale chemical ordering.
The short-aging-induced ordering modestly increases strength.
Short aging retains toughness by preserving dislocation mobility and crack-blunting behavior.
Aging for more than 5 hours at approximately 500°C coarsens clusters or forms brittle secondary precipitates.
The products of extended aging localize stress and cause a marked loss of toughness.
The controlled intervention is aging at 500°C for 0.5, 2, 5, or 10 hours followed by rapid quenching.
The relevant structural mediator is the balance between nanoscale chemical ordering and discrete intragranular or grain-boundary nanoprecipitates.
Uniform subtle ordering or nanoclustering impedes dislocation motion enough to enhance strength without compromising toughness.
Coarsened clusters or brittle secondary phases inhibit dislocation mobility.
Coarsened clusters or brittle secondary phases act as crack-initiation sites and promote localized cleavage.
Relative to the rapidly quenched baseline, samples aged for less than 2 hours will have modestly higher strength while maintaining toughness.
Relative to the rapidly quenched baseline, samples aged for more than 5 hours will exhibit a pronounced decrease in toughness.
After more than 5 hours of aging, strength may saturate or decline slightly as brittle precipitates form.
Mechanical-property changes will correlate directly with a microstructural transition from subtle ordering to evident precipitation.
The rapidly quenched baseline is a homogeneous single-phase CoCrFeMnNi solid solution without advanced chemical ordering or secondary precipitates.
The hypothesis is limited to moderate aging temperatures around 500°C and alloys that are initially single-phase solid solutions.
Changes in composition, temperature, or processing that produce a multiphase starting state may place the system outside the hypothesis's domain.
Variations in initial microstructure or experimental conditions may shift the aging duration at which beneficial ordering changes to deleterious precipitation.
